name: Ion (not the tragic poet)
bio: Ion (not the tragic poet) is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no date for the poet.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 43, 44).

poems.title: Book VII, 43: On Euripides
poems.author: Ion (not the tragic poet)
poems.text: Hail, Euripides, dwelling in the chamber of eternal night in the dark-robed valleys of Pieria! Know, though thou art under earth, that thy renown shall be everlasting, equal to the perennial charm of Homer.

poems.title: Book VII, 44: On the Same
poems.author: Ion (not the tragic poet)
poems.text: Though a tearful fate befel thee, O Euripides, devoured by wolf-hounds, thou, the honey-voiced nightingale of the stage, the ornament of Athens, who didst mingle the grace of the Muses with wisdom, yet thou wast laid in the tomb at Pella, that the servant of the Pierian Muses should dwell near the home of his mistresses.
